labs.title: Plan repository work with Issues, milestones, and Projects
labs.summary: Create GitHub issues from templates, organize them with a milestone and labels, track them in a Project with a priority field, and link a pull request with a closing keyword.
labs.scenario: Contoso Labs is preparing **contoso-labs/inventory-api** for the v1.2 release. In the simulated GitHub repository, create a **v1.2** milestone, open a bug and feature request from the template chooser, add both issues to a new Projects board named **Inventory API roadmap**, prioritize the items, save a milestone-filtered view, and link pull request **#14** with **Closes #21**. Everything is simulated.
learningObjectives: Create issues from templates with assignees, labels, and milestones
Use GitHub Projects templates, Status values, custom fields, and saved views
Link pull requests to issues with closing keywords
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with repositories, issues, and pull requests

sources.title: Linking a pull request to an issue

components.title: Planning surfaces
components.text: Use **Issues** for trackable work, **Milestones** for release-sized groups of issues and pull requests, and **Projects** for flexible table, board, and roadmap planning. Use **Discussions** for open-ended Q&A or community conversation rather than assigned work.

components.title: README.md
components.content:
# Inventory API

Fictional service for GitHub planning labs.

Release v1.2 focuses on CSV imports and stock notifications.

components.text: Issues can include labels, milestones, assignees, and sub-issues. Labels categorize work; milestones track progress for a release; sub-issues break a larger item into smaller work.

components.text: Projects is the current flexible planning experience. A project can have **Table**, **Board**, and **Roadmap** views, custom fields, filters, grouping, and templates. It replaces classic projects for most planning work.

components.title: Choose a project template
components.description: Board is the best start for release triage; Table and Roadmap are alternate layouts you can explain to stakeholders.

components.text: A pull request description that contains a closing keyword such as `Closes #21` closes that issue when the pull request merges.

components.title: Issues vs Discussions
components.text: Discussions are for conversations and Q&A. Issues are for actionable work with metadata, milestones, projects, and pull request links.

pullRequests.title: Validate CSV import rows
pullRequests.description: Adds validation for CSV import rows and clearer errors.

steps.title: Create the v1.2 milestone
steps.instruction: Open **Issues**, select **Milestones**, select **New milestone**, then create **v1.2** with due date **2026-10-30**.
steps.explanation: Milestones group issues and pull requests for a release and show progress.

steps.title: Create template-based issues
steps.instruction: Use **New issue** to create a **Bug report** assigned to **alex-contoso** with labels **bug** and **good first issue**, and a **Feature request** assigned to **sam-contoso** with label **enhancement**. Add both to **v1.2**.
steps.hint: The template chooser has Bug report and Feature request cards.
steps.explanation: Templates gather consistent details; labels, assignees, and milestones add planning metadata.

rules.failureFeedback: Create bug issue #21 with assignee, labels, and milestone.
Create feature issue #22 with enhancement label and v1.2 milestone.

steps.title: Create a Projects board
steps.instruction: Open **Projects**, select **New project**, choose **Board**, and name it **Inventory API roadmap**. Table and Roadmap are alternate views you can use later.
steps.hint: Use the Board template, not a classic project.
steps.explanation: Projects is the flexible planning tool for board, table, and roadmap views.

rules.failureFeedback: Create the Board project named Inventory API roadmap.

steps.title: Add Priority and issues to the project
steps.instruction: In the project, create a **Single select** field named **Priority**. Add issue **#21** with **Status** In Progress and **Priority** High; add **#22** with **Status** Todo and **Priority** Medium.
steps.hint: Create Priority before adding project items.
steps.explanation: Status shows workflow state; a single-select Priority field keeps values consistent.

rules.failureFeedback: Create Priority as a single-select field.
Add issue #21 with In Progress and High.
Add issue #22 with Todo and Medium.

steps.title: Create a milestone-filtered view
steps.instruction: Create a view named **v1.2 by priority** using **Table**, grouped by **Priority**, with filter **milestone:v1.2**.
steps.hint: Saved views let teams switch perspectives without changing the underlying work.
steps.explanation: A priority-grouped table helps release triage while the board still supports status tracking.

rules.failureFeedback: Create the v1.2 by priority view.

steps.title: Link the pull request
steps.instruction: Open **Pull requests**, open **#14**, and update the description to include **Closes #21**.
steps.hint: Closing keywords close the linked issue after merge.
steps.explanation: Linking PRs and issues connects code review with planning status.

finalRules.description: Issue is in project with milestone and priority, and PR closes it
finalRules.successFeedback: The issue is planned and linked to the pull request.
finalRules.failureFeedback: Ensure #21 has milestone and priority in the project, and PR #14 includes Closes #21.

labs.solution:
1. Open **Issues** > **Milestones** > **New milestone** and create `v1.2` due `2026-10-30`.
2. Open **Issues** > **New issue**. Choose **Bug report**, enter the CSV title/body, set **Assignees** to `alex-contoso`, labels `bug` and `good first issue`, and **Milestone** `v1.2`.
3. Choose **Feature request**, enter the low-stock title/body, set **Assignees** to `sam-contoso`, label `enhancement`, and **Milestone** `v1.2`.
4. Open **Projects** > **New project**, choose **Board**, and name it `Inventory API roadmap`.
5. In the project, use **New field** to create **Priority** as **Single select** with High, Medium, Low.
6. Use **Add item** to add `#21` as **In Progress** / **High** and `#22` as **Todo** / **Medium**.
7. Use **New view** to create `v1.2 by priority` as a **Table** grouped by **Priority** with filter `milestone:v1.2`.
8. Open **Pull requests** > **#14** and update the description with `Closes #21`.
